items.title: Invasion Day bomb declared terror act, as accused's 'pro-white ideology' probed
items.description: The attempted bombing of an Invasion Day rally in Perth's CBD last week is declared a terrorist attack by authorities.

items.title: Nationals issue Ley with reunion counteroffer as deadline looms
items.description: The minor party has given the opposition leader terms that one Nationals MP said they did "not expect" would be acceptable in what has been described as a bid to push out her self-imposed deadline.

items.title: How capital gains tax changes could impact you
items.description: According to a well-sourced leak, changes to capital gains tax discounts could form the centrepiece of the next federal budget in May. And while the government has downplayed the idea, it has not been ruled out.

items.title: Gus disappearance declared major crime, suspect identified
items.description: South Australian police have declared the disappearance of Gus Lamont a major crime and say a person who lives at his outback property is now considered a suspect, but have stressed that the boy's parents are not under investigation.

items.title: A Republican stronghold has turned blue — is it a 'warning' to Trump?
items.description: The US has been gripped by cold weather in recent weeks, but pundits say it is in Texas where hell has truly frozen over. A blue wave just swept a GOP stronghold, and Republicans are very worried.

items.title: Andrew Hastie brought an intriguing book into Parliament
items.description: The calamity unfolding in the dissolved Coalition provided a convenient distraction for the government, which should have had a worse week amid an interest rate hike.

items.title: Could this supported housing model for the homeless prevent a future tragedy?
items.description: An inquest into the Bondi Junction stabbing has recommended that the NSW government support long-term accommodation for homeless people experiencing mental health issues. It's a model that is already finding success.

items.title: Questions about Randa Abdel-Fattah inclusion in NSW writers festival
items.description: The NSW government makes contact with the board of next month's Newcastle Writers Festival about the inclusion of Palestinian author Randa Abdel-Fattah, the ABC understands.

items.title: British billionaire urged to accept $350 million for mothballed mine
items.description: The Mining and Energy Union says a firm $350 million offer is on the table to restart Tahmoor Colliery, warning delays risk the mine's future and hundreds of jobs.

items.title: Ruling made in Bunnings' three-year fight to use AI to scan customer faces
items.description: Bunnings was reasonably entitled to use AI facial recognition technology to combat crime and staff abuse in its stores, the Administrative Review Tribunal finds.

items.title: Today show host Savannah Guthrie asks for proof her mother is alive
items.description: NBC's Today show host Savannah Guthrie says her family is ready to talk to people holding their mother, but they want to see proof that she is alive.

items.title: 'Hijacked by left-wing extremists': Calls for Mardi Gras funding review
items.description: The cancellation of the LGBTQIA+ parade's afterparty has escalated to the NSW parliament, with the Pride in Protest group being accused of threatening the viability of the event.

items.title: Mother of autistic children shares story in wake of WA family tragedy
items.description: A mother of two autistic children living in regional Western Australia has shared her experience of navigating bureaucracy while caring for children with complex needs.

items.title: Alleged attempted murder victim tells of 'cat-and-mouse' chase around office
items.description: A woman who was stabbed multiple times in an alleged attack which killed her colleague at an Adelaide real estate office tells a court of her “fight for life”. Warning: This story contains content some readers may find distressing.

items.title: Man convicted of sexually assaulting two girls at Canberra Reptile Zoo
items.description: A 26-year-old man has been convicted in the ACT Supreme Court of sexually assaulting two girls at Canberra Reptile Zoo.

items.title: Star Wars hero Daisy Ridley is ready to battle Australian zombies
items.description: These Final Hours writer and director Zak Hilditch drew on personal tragedy to produce We Bury the Dead, his biggest cinematic epic yet.

items.title: Chaos returns to MCG after 'unsatisfactory' Boxing Day Test
items.description: After the two-day Ashes Test raised eyebrows over the MCG pitch, Queensland and Victoria are on track for another swift finish after 17 wickets on day one of their Sheffield Shield clash.

items.title: 'Max should not have died': Teen's family react to coronial findings
items.description: The coroner could not definitively rule that the anaphylaxis death of 15-year-old Max McKenzie was preventable, despite identifying delays in the teen's medical treatment.

items.title: Private health insurers take aim at rising specialists fees in new report
items.description: A survey of 4,000 patients finds more than half had an unexpected cost when under a specialist's care.

items.title: Spirit of Tasmania ferry operator facing 'substantial loss'
items.description: Ferry operator TT-Line is confident its two new Spirit of Tasmania vessels will begin operating by October — but it says there is a "risk" its existing ships might not be sold by then.

items.title: Worker's death at Central Australian gold mine under investigation
items.description: A 47-year-old worker has died following an incident at the Tanami gold mine in remote Central Australia, with police and NT WorkSafe investigating.

items.title: 'Incredible pieces of real estate': Sale of Perth barracks draws huge interest
items.description: The planned sale of the Irwin and Leeuwin barracks in Perth will see dozens of hectares of potentially prime residential land hit the market. So is it likely to be used for housing, and what difference will it really make?

items.title: 'There will be strikes': Unions pushing above-inflation wage increases
items.description: Australia's biggest employers are under pressure to give their workers pay increases above 4 per cent this year, as real wages go backwards and the union movement ramps up pressure.

items.title: Queensland mayor pleads guilty to breaching bail with cup of tea in casino
items.description: A Far North Queensland mayor has pleaded guilty to two counts of breaching his bail conditions after he was found drinking tea in a casino with a person he must avoid.

items.title: Arnie's owner weeps as he's sentenced over dog's ute death
items.description: A Queensland man who claimed his dog Arnie had been stolen, despite having left the German shepherd in his car, where it was later found dead, has pleaded guilty.
